findings.body: `canManage()` returns true for a view-only grant, allowing the administrator to create groups despite lacking the `manage` scope.
findings.failure_mode: Authorization succeeds for a mutation that the assigned scope is not intended to permit.
findings.impact: `canManage()` returns true for a view-only grant, allowing the administrator to create groups despite lacking the `manage` scope.
findings.root_cause: The global manage check treats the read-only `view` scope as equivalent to `manage`.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` in `canManage()`, and update its Javadoc and tests so a `view`-only all-groups permission is explicitly rejected for group creation.
findings.title: A view-only all-groups permission grants group creation
findings.trigger: A same-realm administrator has an all-groups permission containing only the `view` scope and invokes an operation guarded by `groups().requireManage()`, such as POSTing a new top-level group.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 70 verbatim shows `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);` in `canManage()`. The method name implies only MANAGE scope should grant permission, but VIEW is also accepted. This allows view-only grants to pass canManage() checks, enabling group creation with insufficient privileges.

findings.body: The documentation claims the method returns a stream even though its declared return type is `Set<String>`, giving callers incorrect information about laziness, reuse, and collection semantics.
findings.evidence: * @return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.
findings.failure_mode: Generated API documentation misstates the method contract.
findings.impact: The documentation claims the method returns a stream even though its declared return type is `Set<String>`, giving callers incorrect information about laziness, reuse, and collection semantics.
findings.root_cause: The newly added Javadoc uses the wrong collection type name.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the return documentation to say that the method returns a set of group IDs with view-member permission.
findings.title: The return documentation incorrectly describes a Set as a Stream
findings.trigger: A developer consults the generated API documentation for `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 145 shows `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.` but line 147 declares `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. The Javadoc incorrectly states Stream when the return type is Set, providing incorrect API documentation.

findings.body: The documentation points to membership-management authorization rather than member-management authorization, obscuring which scope causes the method to throw.
findings.failure_mode: API documentation describes a different authorization check from the one executed.
findings.impact: The documentation points to membership-management authorization rather than member-management authorization, obscuring which scope causes the method to throw.
findings.root_cause: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers` was copied from the adjacent membership method without updating the referenced predicate.
findings.title: `requireManageMembers` documents the wrong predicate
findings.trigger: A developer uses the interface documentation to determine which permission predicate controls `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)`.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines 132-134 show `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` for requireManageMembers. This should reference canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. The Javadoc documents the wrong predicate.

raw_findings.body: The individual authorization resource created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` is not assigned the `Groups` resource type, so this query omits it and the authorized group's ID is not supplied to the user provider; authorized users are missing from searches and counts.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Type-based lookup silently returns no per-group authorization resources.
raw_findings.impact: The individual authorization resource created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` is not assigned the `Groups` resource type, so this query omits it and the authorized group's ID is not supplied to the user provider; authorized users are missing from searches and counts.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new enumeration assumes individual group authorization resources carry `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, while the schema creation path only creates the resource and updates its scopes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When creating schema-backed resources, assign the supplied schema resource type to the resource before relying on `findByType`, and add a test that retrieves a newly created per-group resource through this query.
raw_findings.title: Per-group resources are enumerated by a type that is never assigned during schema creation
raw_findings.trigger: A V2 scope permission is created for an individual group and an administrator without global user-view permission subsequently searches or counts users through group-member permissions.

raw_findings.body: `hasPermission` looks up the generated authorization-resource ID as a resource name, and any returned set also contains generated resource IDs rather than realm group IDs. User-provider membership queries therefore fail to match the authorized groups and omit their users.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Permission evaluation and downstream group-membership filtering use identifiers from the wrong domain.
raw_findings.impact: `hasPermission` looks up the generated authorization-resource ID as a resource name, and any returned set also contains generated resource IDs rather than realm group IDs. User-provider membership queries therefore fail to match the authorized groups and omit their users.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation conflates the authorization model's generated `Resource.getId()` with the represented `GroupModel.getId()` stored as the resource name.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the already loaded `groupResource` directly and add its name, which is the resolved realm group ID, to `granted`; alternatively persist an explicit group-ID attribute and return that value.
raw_findings.title: Authorization resource IDs are mistaken for realm group IDs
raw_findings.trigger: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates an individual group authorization resource created with a generated authorization-resource ID and a name equal to the realm group ID.

raw_findings.body: Only authorization resources are enumerated, so ordinary realm groups are absent from the returned group-ID set. Counts can incorrectly return zero, and searches can omit users belonging to groups not represented by individual resources.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A global group-member grant is converted into an incomplete membership filter.
raw_findings.impact: Only authorization resources are enumerated, so ordinary realm groups are absent from the returned group-ID set. Counts can incorrectly return zero, and searches can omit users belonging to groups not represented by individual resources.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation derives the universe of visible realm groups from sparsely created authorization resources rather than from the realm group model when a type-wide permission applies.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Detect an effective all-groups member permission and enumerate the realm's actual group IDs, or change the method contract to represent global group-member visibility explicitly so user count/search paths do not apply an incomplete ID filter.
raw_findings.title: All-groups member permissions do not produce IDs for groups without individual resources
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator receives `view-members` or `manage-members` on the all-groups resource, while one or more realm groups have no individual authorization resource, and then calls the user count or search endpoint.

raw_findings.body: Because the individual resource is non-null, the method never evaluates the all-groups resource. The administrator is incorrectly denied viewing or managing that group even though the type-wide permission should apply to every group.
raw_findings.evidence: Resource resource = groupId == null ? null : resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId);
raw_findings.failure_mode: Creating any individual group resource changes and narrows the effective behavior of an unrelated global permission.
raw_findings.impact: Because the individual resource is non-null, the method never evaluates the all-groups resource. The administrator is incorrectly denied viewing or managing that group even though the type-wide permission should apply to every group.
raw_findings.root_cause: The all-groups permission is implemented as a resource-existence fallback instead of an authorization fallback.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the individual resource first and, if it does not grant the requested scope, also evaluate the all-groups resource rather than using it only when the individual resource is absent.
raw_findings.title: An individual resource suppresses otherwise applicable all-groups permissions
raw_findings.trigger: An individual authorization resource already exists for a group because of any group-specific policy, while the current administrator is granted the requested scope only through the all-groups resource.

validated_findings.root_cause: The implementation derives the universe of visible realm groups from sparsely created authorization resources rather than from the realm group model when a type-wide permission applies.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Detect an effective all-groups member permission and enumerate the realm's actual group IDs, or change the method contract to represent global group-member visibility explicitly so user count/search paths do not apply an incomplete ID filter.
validated_findings.title: All-groups member permissions do not produce IDs for groups without individual resources
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator receives `view-members` or `manage-members` on the all-groups resource, while one or more realm groups have no individual authorization resource, and then calls the user count or search endpoint.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about all-groups permissions not producing IDs for groups without individual resources conflates two issues. The method iterates authorization resources by type, which is the intended design for V2 permissions. The actual bug is the ID confusion (candidate 2), not missing realm groups.

validated_findings.body: Because the individual resource is non-null, the method never evaluates the all-groups resource. The administrator is incorrectly denied viewing or managing that group even though the type-wide permission should apply to every group.
validated_findings.evidence: Resource resource = groupId == null ? null : resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId);
validated_findings.failure_mode: Creating any individual group resource changes and narrows the effective behavior of an unrelated global permission.
validated_findings.impact: Because the individual resource is non-null, the method never evaluates the all-groups resource. The administrator is incorrectly denied viewing or managing that group even though the type-wide permission should apply to every group.
validated_findings.root_cause: The all-groups permission is implemented as a resource-existence fallback instead of an authorization fallback.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the individual resource first and, if it does not grant the requested scope, also evaluate the all-groups resource rather than using it only when the individual resource is absent.
validated_findings.title: An individual resource suppresses otherwise applicable all-groups permissions
validated_findings.trigger: An individual authorization resource already exists for a group because of any group-specific policy, while the current administrator is granted the requested scope only through the all-groups resource.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 141 shows `Resource resource = groupId == null ? null : resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId);`. When an individual resource exists (resource != null), lines 143-150 show the all-groups fallback only triggers when resource is null. An existing individual resource suppresses evaluation of all-groups permissions, denying access that should be granted.

validated_findings.body: Existing source no longer compiles, and previously compiled callers can fail with `NoSuchMethodError` because the public interface method was removed without a compatibility bridge.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Binary and source compatibility are broken for external interface consumers.
validated_findings.impact: Existing source no longer compiles, and previously compiled callers can fail with `NoSuchMethodError` because the public interface method was removed without a compatibility bridge.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch deletes a method from a public interface instead of deprecating and bridging it to the replacement.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Retain the old method as a deprecated default method delegating to `canViewMembers(group)`, then remove it only in a documented incompatible release.
validated_findings.title: Removing the per-group evaluator method breaks existing interface consumers
validated_findings.trigger: An extension or separately compiled module calls the public `GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` method after upgrading to this version.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows LEFT side line 49 removing `boolean getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group)`. However, this is an internal SPI interface, and Keycloak's versioning policy for experimental features (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2) does not guarantee binary compatibility. The claim of breaking external consumers is ungrounded without evidence of public API contract.

validated_findings.body: Old callers can fail with `NoSuchMethodError`, while implementations that only provide the former abstract method can fail with `AbstractMethodError` when the new method is invoked.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The interface's binary contract changes incompatibly across the upgrade.
validated_findings.impact: Old callers can fail with `NoSuchMethodError`, while implementations that only provide the former abstract method can fail with `AbstractMethodError` when the new method is invoked.
validated_findings.root_cause: An abstract public interface method was renamed without a default compatibility adapter.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the old signature during a compatibility period and introduce the new name through a default bridge; alternatively defer the rename to a documented major compatibility break.
validated_findings.title: Renaming the group-ID set method breaks callers and existing implementations
validated_findings.trigger: A separately compiled caller invokes the old no-argument method, or an existing implementation of `GroupPermissionEvaluator` is used by new code that invokes `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Similar to candidate 5, the rename from getGroupsWithViewPermission() to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is in an internal SPI interface for an experimental feature. Without evidence this is a public stable API, the compatibility break claim is ungrounded.

validated_findings.body: The documentation claims the method returns a stream even though its declared return type is `Set<String>`, giving callers incorrect information about laziness, reuse, and collection semantics.
validated_findings.evidence: * @return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Generated API documentation misstates the method contract.
validated_findings.impact: The documentation claims the method returns a stream even though its declared return type is `Set<String>`, giving callers incorrect information about laziness, reuse, and collection semantics.
validated_findings.root_cause: The newly added Javadoc uses the wrong collection type name.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Change the return documentation to say that the method returns a set of group IDs with view-member permission.
validated_findings.title: The return documentation incorrectly describes a Set as a Stream
validated_findings.trigger: A developer consults the generated API documentation for `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 145 shows `@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission.` but line 147 declares `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`. The Javadoc incorrectly states Stream when the return type is Set, providing incorrect API documentation.

validated_findings.body: The documentation points to membership-management authorization rather than member-management authorization, obscuring which scope causes the method to throw.
validated_findings.failure_mode: API documentation describes a different authorization check from the one executed.
validated_findings.impact: The documentation points to membership-management authorization rather than member-management authorization, obscuring which scope causes the method to throw.
validated_findings.root_cause: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers` was copied from the adjacent membership method without updating the referenced predicate.
validated_findings.title: `requireManageMembers` documents the wrong predicate
validated_findings.trigger: A developer uses the interface documentation to determine which permission predicate controls `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 132-134 show `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` for requireManageMembers. This should reference canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. The Javadoc documents the wrong predicate.
